list.cause: Lifting off the throttle mid-corner (lift-off oversteer)
list.detail: You came off the throttle from 91% to 0% while turning. That shifts weight forward and the rear loses grip.
list.fix: Avoid sudden lifts mid-corner. If you are too fast, ease off gently or brake earlier next lap.

corners.name: T1
corners.tip: Slow in, fast out: do all your braking in a straight line, turn in late, apex late, then get to full throttle as early as the exit allows.

corners.name: T2

corners.name: T3

findings.title: T3: you lose 0.74 s per lap on average vs your best pass
findings.detail: your fastest pass carried 3.3 km/h more minimum speed.

findings.title: T2: you lose 0.55 s per lap on average vs your best pass

findings.title: T1: you lose 0.35 s per lap on average vs your best pass

findings.title: T1: 42 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T2: 40 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T1: tighter at the apex but 1.3 m wider on exit than your best lap
findings.detail: That is an early apex: you cut in too soon, then run out of road on exit and must wait for the throttle. Turn in later so the apex comes later.

findings.title: T2: brake released abruptly while turning
findings.detail: Snapping off the brake while turning unloads the front tyres and causes entry understeer. Trail off the brake gradually toward the apex.

findings.title: T3: brake released abruptly while turning
findings.detail: Snapping off the brake while turning unloads the front tyres and causes entry understeer. Trail off the brake gradually toward the apex.

findings.title: T1: throttle lifted again after picking it up
findings.detail: Picking up the throttle and then lifting usually means you got on it too early or too hard. Squeeze it on smoothly once, and only add more.

findings.title: T2: 2 steering corrections per pass
findings.detail: You keep re-adjusting the wheel mid-corner, which usually means the car is sliding or you turned in at the wrong point. Aim for one smooth input in and one smooth unwind out.

findings.title: T3: throttle lifted again after picking it up
findings.detail: Picking up the throttle and then lifting usually means you got on it too early or too hard. Squeeze it on smoothly once, and only add more.

setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: Front ride height under 1 cm for 46.6% of the time at speed
setup.detail: The car is probably touching the ground. Low-downforce cars should not do this; for high-downforce cars some is normal. If the car feels nervous over bumps, kerbs or in fast corners, raise ride height a few mm or stiffen springs/bump stops on that axle.

setup.title: Rear ride height under 1 cm for 58.7% of the time at speed
setup.detail: The car is probably touching the ground. Low-downforce cars should not do this; for high-downforce cars some is normal. If the car feels nervous over bumps, kerbs or in fast corners, raise ride height a few mm or stiffen springs/bump stops on that axle.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 3 of 3 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T2, T3. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T1, T2, T3)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 3 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 63.2% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

pros.title: Very few locked wheels
pros.detail: You are not flat-spotting tyres under braking.

cons.title: Coasting: 16.1% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 82 m per lap in T1, T2. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Throttle on-off-on at the apex (T1, T3)
cons.detail: You pick up the throttle, lift, then reapply. That unsettles the car and usually means you went to the throttle too hard or too early.

cons.title: Brake released abruptly while turning (T2, T3)
cons.detail: Snapping off the brake mid-turn-in unloads the front tyres and causes understeer at the apex.

cons.title: Early apex (T1)
cons.detail: You cut to the inside too soon, then run wide on exit and have to wait before full throttle.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T2)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T3, T2, T1
cons.detail: T3: 0.74 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.55 s between your average and best pass; T1: 0.35 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T1, T2.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T3, T2, T1: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Stabbing the throttle and lifting again
stopDoing.detail: Pick it up once, gently, and only ever add more.

stopDoing.title: Snapping off the brake with the wheel turned
stopDoing.detail: Release it gradually over the last 20-30 m before the apex.

stopDoing.title: Turning in too early
stopDoing.detail: In T1, wait a beat longer before turning so the apex comes later and the exit is straighter.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (16.1% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Check after a few laps to see if you are overheating one end.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Let AMS2 set steering lock for each car, and watch the FFB meter for clipping.

traits.name: Speed
traits.text: Slow. Mistakes happen gently and you have time to react.

traits.name: Cornering grip
traits.text: Modest grip, like a sporty road car.

traits.name: Braking power
traits.text: Weak brakes: brake early and carry momentum instead.

traits.name: Wheelspin tendency
traits.text: The engine can't overpower the tyres: full throttle is almost always safe.

traits.name: Downforce
traits.text: No downforce: grip is the same at any speed.

traits.name: How forgiving
traits.text: Very forgiving; ideal for learning lines and braking points.

tips: Low grip: brake in a straight line, turn smoothly, and avoid sudden inputs.
